tagline: A whole is not simply a set with better furniture
definition: The study of parts and wholes, including how things compose larger things, whether parts can overlap, and what principles govern the relationship between an entity and what belongs to it.
etymology: From Greek meros, part, and -logy, study or account; the term names inquiry into the formal relations of parts and wholes.

sections.heading: The question of parthood
sections.text: Mereology asks how parts relate to wholes and to one another. A spoke belongs to a wheel, and the wheel belongs to a bicycle. Many systems treat parthood as transitive, so that the spoke is also part of the bicycle, while distinguishing ordinary from proper parthood.

sections.heading: Overlap and composition
sections.text: Two things overlap when they share a part in the relevant system. Composition asks a further question: under what conditions do some things together form another thing? Philosophers disagree about whether any collection composes a whole or whether connection, function, life, or other restrictions are required.

sections.heading: Membership is a different relation
sections.text: An element's membership in a set does not automatically behave like parthood. If a person belongs to a committee and that committee belongs to an association, set membership alone does not imply the person is a member of the association. Confusing the relations erases their distinct formal roles.

sections.heading: Boundaries carry commitments
sections.text: An organism, an orchestra, and a heap invite different intuitions about what counts as a component or a whole. Mereology helps make those intuitions explicit. It does not guarantee that one everyday criterion resolves every case or that spatial contact alone settles questions of identity and composition.

literary: The wheel claimed the spoke, the bicycle claimed the wheel, and the journey, which owned none of them, assembled their separate circles into the temporary wholeness of arrival.
art_caption: A wheel, its smaller assembly, and one detached spoke stage different levels of parthood without equating parts with set members.
